citeAs: Clark, C., Lee, K., Chang, M.-W., Kwiatkowski, T., Collins, M., & Toutanova, K. (2019). BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions. arXiv preprint arXiv:1905.10044.
creator: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova (University of Washington, Google AI Language)
description: A reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions generated in unprompted and unconstrained settings, paired with Wikipedia passages.
name: BoolQ
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Three authors labelled 110 randomly chosen examples to assess annotation quality, reaching 90% accuracy compared to gold-standard labels.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators decide if the question is good (comprehensible, unambiguous, requesting factual information). Then they find a passage within the document containing the answer, or mark it 'not answerable'. Finally, they mark whether the answer is 'yes' or 'no'.
rai:dataBiases: Class imbalance: 'Yes' answers are slightly more common (62.31% in the train set).
rai:dataCollection: Questions are gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine. Queries are heuristically filtered for yes/no questions. Questions are kept if a Wikipedia page is returned in the top 5 results. Human annotators then process the question/article pairs.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotators can mark questions as 'not answerable' if the Wikipedia article does not contain the requested information.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine and Wikipedia articles.
rai:dataLimitations: Question-only models perform very poorly on this task, confirming questions do not contain sufficient information to predict the answer on their own.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries heuristically identified by checking if the first word is in a manually constructed set of indicator words and are of sufficient length. Questions only kept if a Wikipedia page is returned as one of the first five results.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing models on their ability to answer naturally occurring yes/no questions and highly inferential reading comprehension.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic identification of yes/no questions using a manually constructed set of indicator words.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Questions are gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine.

null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Not explicitly named in the paper.
